author: DAN EAKIN The Lufkin Daily News
title: EAKIN: A tornado put a man on the right path | Community News | lufkindailynews.com
text:
Jimmy Jones never lived in Deep East Texas.
But between 1995 and 2002, he, his sister Connie Perry and daughter Mary Fay Jackson were seen by thousands of people in this area and by millions around the world on the Daystar Television Network.
During those years they were on television after starting the Texas Country Gospel Music program and sang as 1 A Chord.
In 1999, the Jones Family Theatre opened in Farmers Branch, on the north edge of Dallas. I worked for the Metrocrest News which ran in the Dallas Morning News on Thursdays in Farmers Branch, Carrollton, Lewisville and Coppell.
1 A Chord opened at the Jones Family Theatre for the Saturday night Grand Ole Opry style programs, which featured some of the best known gospel music groups in America.
One afternoon, I was sitting backstage talking with Jimmy Jones when he told me the story of how he and his family began the full time gospel music ministry.
He said he owned rock sites at several locations in Texas and had a small airplane which he used to fly from one rock site to the other.
One night he and an employee were flying, with Jimmy as the pilot, toward a location near Texarkana. While near Paris, Texas, he said a tornado developed, and they found themselves in the middle of it.
He said he kept fighting to keep the airplane to keep from spinning in the tornado when he heard a voice saying, “Jimmy! Just let it go!”
He said he just threw both hands up in the air, and the tornado threw the plane out. The two men were safe, but the plane had lost its lights and the radio equipment was not working.
For some time after that, he and his employee were in flight in almost total darkness, not knowing if they were going north, south, east or west.
Eventually, the clouds disappeared and there was some light from the moon and stars. They were somewhere in East Texas.
He said he saw a gravel road leading up to a farm house and told his friend, “I think I can set the plane down on that road.”
He did. He said the plane traveled up the gravel road and then made a sharp left at the farm house. He said the right wing of the plane landed on the front porch and he and his partner stepped out of the plane right onto the porch.
They knocked on the door. A woman came to the door and said, “I just told my husband there is an airplane on our front porch and he said, ‘Woman, you’re crazy’!”
He said he told the woman, “We just thought we’d drop in for supper.”
They were fed and the friendly farm couple said they could spend the night and take care of the airplane the next day.
“That night, I laid on the bed in that farm house looking at the ceiling,” he said. “I told myself, Jimmy Jones, you have millions of dollars in the bank, and here you are trying to make more.”
He added, “That night I made a decision that I would no longer spend my life laying up treasure on earth, but I would spend the rest of my life laying up treasure in heaven.”
His family was already enjoying singing gospel music but had not yet been performing much in public. They began The Texas Country Gospel Music program on the Daystar Television Network and as 1 A Chord, Jimmy, Connie and Mary Fay were soon being seen and heard around the world.
Jesus, in Matthew 6:19-20, said, “Lay not up for yourselves treasures on earth where moth and rust doth corrupt and thieves break through and steal, but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven where neither moth nor dust doth corrupt and where thieves do not break through nor steal.”
It had taken a tornado to put Jimmy Jones on the right path.
He died on Oct. 6, 2021 at age 83. I spoke at his funeral in Gainesville and told the story of the tornado to the crowd that had come to celebrate his life. He was one of the most wonderful men I ever knew.
Mary Fay continues to host the Texas Country Gospel Music program every week on at least 25 different television stations.
The program can also be seen on You Tube and at the Texas Country Gospel Music Program website.
